title: Suffices on the convenient I n-scaled integral for the Catalan integral formula
intent: Prove the Catalan integral formula (the density x powr (real n - 1/2) * sqrt (4 - x) / (2*pi) has integral real (catalan n) over {0..4}) by first proving the more convenient statement in terms of the auxiliary integral I n — the same density times inverse (2*pi) integrates to I n * inverse (2*pi) — and then rewriting I n / (2*pi) to real (catalan n) through the bridge lemma catalan_eq_I.

parent.name: catalan_integral_form
parent.statement:
theorem catalan_integral_form:
  "((\<lambda>x. x powr (real n - 1 / 2) * sqrt (4 - x) / (2*pi)) 
       has_integral real (catalan n)) {0..4}"

children.name: integrable_I
children.statement:
private lemma integrable_I: 
  "(\<lambda>x. x powr (of_nat n - 1/2) * sqrt (4 - x)) integrable_on {0..4}"
children.closed_by: proof (cases "n = 0"); case True closed by has_integral_I0 via has_integral_integrable; case False closed by integrable_continuous_real continuous_on_mult continuous_on_powr' (auto intro!: continuous_intros)

children.name: catalan_eq_I
children.statement: private lemma catalan_eq_I: "real (catalan n) = I n / (2 * pi)"
children.closed_by: proof (induction n); base case 0 by has_integral_I0 with I_def integral_unique; step case by of_nat_catalan_Suc' Suc.IH I_Suc

applicability.goal_shape: An identity whose right-hand side involves a constant you also have an auxiliary definition for (here the unnormalized integral I n), so the goal can be restated in terms of that auxiliary quantity and then bridged back by one rewrite; concretely a `... has_integral real (catalan n) {0..4}` goal with a normalizing constant 1/(2*pi).
applicability.use_when: the more convenient statement is genuinely easier than the original (here it needs only integrability integrable_I plus the rule has_integral_mult_left), and the bridge identity (catalan_eq_I) is already proved or provable on its own; the constant you rewrite away has an established equivalence with the goal's constant.
applicability.avoid_when: the bridge identity is the hard part and is not already available (then the suffices just moves the difficulty without reducing it); the convenient statement is not actually easier; or the goal can be closed by a single direct rule so the detour through the auxiliary quantity adds nothing.

consequences: The move creates two obligations from one: (a) the convenient restatement must be proved, which here needs the integrability premise integrable_I and the scaling rule has_integral_mult_left; (b) the bridge identity catalan_eq_I must hold, and it is the only place the reader sees why the result is about the Catalan number at all. Failure modes: if the bridge constant were wrong (a sign or normalization error in catalan_eq_I), the final `simp add: catalan_eq_I field_simps` would fail or rewrite to the wrong value; and if integrable_I were stated for the wrong exponent, the `intro ... integrable_I` step in the convenient statement would not apply.
